items.title: Almost every harmonic-gradient trajectory leaves a finite-volume domain in finite forward time unless the harmonic potential is constant
items.source_title: Jelentés a 2010. évi Schweitzer Miklós Matematikai Emlékversenyről

items.difficulty_reason: The author uses the measurable forward-complete initial set and incompressibility to make an invariant superlevel set at a noncritical density point, then uses strict increase near that point to force strict loss of its finite volume.

dedup.scope: 196562 concerns p-biharmonic maps from a Ricci soliton, and 2056 classifies positive harmonic functions on a discrete group. Neither has forward-time completeness of gradient trajectories on a finite-volume domain.

source_caveats: The problem is printed for R^2, with the proof explicitly in R^n. Keep the report's printed compact exhaustion display, including its apparent intersection/union inconsistency with the immediately preceding existential description.
